pattern: polyester polyol + PPG425 + tackifying resin + MDI
agent_hint: Tackifying-resin-modified PUR is an externally documented formulation family; do not restrict the search to fully reactive polyol/isocyanate mixtures.
limitation: Single patent example; does not report thermal-hold drift.

pattern: multiple polyester polyols + PPG425 + hydrocarbon resin + MDI
agent_hint: Hydrocarbon resin can coexist with reactive PUR while retaining measurable melt-processability; include a minor tackifier/hydrocarbon-resin axis rather than fixing the modifier at zero.
limitation: Different polyols and application; no thermal-hold stability trajectory.

pattern: polyoxypropylene diol + polyester diols + acrylic tackifying resin + MDI
agent_hint: Acrylic-tackifying-resin-modified PUR around 20% of the total formulation is externally documented; 20% is therefore a defensible coarse candidate level, not a value inferred from the local follow-up result.
limitation: Different molecular weights, catalysts and application; viscosity is a single-temperature observation, not a hold-stability measurement.

pattern: polyoxypropylene diol + polyester diols + acrylic tackifying resin + MDI
agent_hint: Repeated examples independently anchor an acrylic-resin design level near 20% while preserving melt processability.
limitation: Different chemistry and process history; no causal stability proof.

pattern: polyoxypropylene diol + polyester diols + acrylic tackifying resin + MDI
agent_hint: The external database supports an acrylic-modified formulation family and provides a reproducible anchor around 20% for coarse candidate generation.
limitation: External analogue only; not evidence for the current formulation's exact optimum.

pattern: polyoxypropylene diol + polyester diols + acrylic tackifying resin + MDI
agent_hint: Multiple neighboring examples reduce the chance that the ~20% acrylic-resin level is a one-off literature artifact.
limitation: No thermal-hold curve and no direct match to AC1920/TK100.

agent_hint: Large viscosity changes across polyol-composition variants show that composition-level changes can strongly alter melt rheology; formulation-family changes are therefore reasonable when the observed failure is large.
limitation: Not a resin-modifier study and not a hold-stability experiment.

pattern: polyether polyol + polyphenylene-ether polyol + acrylic resin + crystalline polyester polyol + MDI
agent_hint: A peer-reviewed PUR study reported 15% acrylic resin as the overall preferred addition level in its system; this independently supports 15% as a coarse acrylic-axis candidate level.
limitation: Optimization target was overall high-temperature adhesive performance, not thermal-hold viscosity; chemistry differs from the local system.

pattern: PPG1000 + PPG2000 + polyester polyol + low-OH acrylic copolymer + MDI
agent_hint: A 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer formulation showed substantially slower viscosity rise than the equal-loading higher-OH acrylic comparator; this supports both a 25% acrylic candidate level and the hypothesis that lower reactive-group density can improve hot-hold stability.
limitation: Different acrylic chemistry and much longer hold window; does not establish the local mechanism.

pattern: same formulation as Example 10 but higher-OH acrylic copolymer
agent_hint: At the same 25 wt% acrylic loading, the higher-OH acrylic analogue exhibited roughly twice the reported 8 h viscosity increase of the low-OH example, making modifier functionality a plausible stability variable rather than loading alone.
limitation: Patent comparison; acrylic materials are not AC1920 and the result is not a direct local-system measurement.

pattern: PPG2025 + PPG4025 + polyester polyol + functional tackifier + MDI
agent_hint: A functional-tackifier-containing formulation had lower reported stability rise than the no-acrylic/no-functional-tackifier comparator in the same example set, supporting the idea that modifier identity can change hot-melt stability.
limitation: Other formulation variables including MDI differ; not an isolated causal comparison.

pattern: PPG2025 + PPG4025 + polyester polyol + MDI; no acrylic polymer or functional tackifier
agent_hint: The no-acrylic/no-functional-tackifier comparator reported a larger stability value than several modifier-containing examples, providing directional support for a modifier-family hypothesis rather than proof of one optimum.
limitation: MDI and other variables differ across the table; use only as directional evidence.

pattern: polyurethane hot melt with optional tackifiers/plasticizers/rheology-control agents
agent_hint: The patent states that tackifiers and rheology-control agents may be used in small amounts, typically below about 10 wt%, supporting 10% as a conservative upper coarse level for the minor-tackifier axis.
limitation: No specific thermal-hold comparison and no exact match to TK100.

pattern: thermally stable reactive hot melt urethane composition
agent_hint: Published formulation art explicitly treats viscosity rise during prolonged hot holding as a design failure mode and cites a preferred stability level of no more than about 25% increase over 4-10 h; this supports thermal-hold stability as an independent design objective.
limitation: The time scale is much longer than the local 15-60 min test and should not be converted into a local numerical threshold.
